results.text:
I read the named files plus `installer.nsi`, `.gitignore`, `rustfmt.toml`, `playwright.config.mjs`, the content packs, and the `cfg(windows)` code paths. Two proposed elements cannot work against the current tree, and the publish order inverts the checks. `Write` is disabled in this session, so the review is below rather than in a plan file.

## VERDICT

Sound shape, wrong sequence, two blocking defects: the prerelease path cannot build a Windows setup file, and the release goes public before anything checks it.

## FINDINGS

**F1 (blocking) — `packaging/windows/installer.nsi:33`.** The line writes `VIProductVersion "${VERSION}.0"`. NSIS accepts four numeric fields only. The version `0.2.0-rc.1` produces `0.2.0-rc.1.0`, and `makensis` stops with an error. Every `-beta.N` tag, every `-rc.N` tag, and every `-dev` build on `main` fails the Windows job. The plan's prerelease stage cannot run today.

**F2 (blocking) — no tag-to-version gate.** `packaging/windows/build.ps1:26` and `packaging/unix/build.sh:28` read the version from `engine-cli --version`. `crates/engine-cli/tests/release_version.rs` ties that printed version to `[workspace.package].version` only. Nothing ties either value to the tag. A tag `v0.3.0` on a tree at `0.2.0` publishes assets named `0.2.0`, and the workflow exits 0. `packaging/unix/smoke.sh:119` compares the program version with the archive name, but both values come from the same binary, so that check is a tautology. The plan's "version match" sits in the post-publish list.

**F3 (blocking ordering) — publish precedes evidence.** The plan publishes on tag push, then runs the Windows clean-machine check locally. The public release therefore exists before any clean-machine evidence exists. Promotion also rebuilds at a new version, so the setup file the sandbox checked is not the file a player downloads. All four post-publish checks (assets, hash round-trip, version, tester smoke) are cheap enough to run before publication.

**F4 — PR checks are Linux-only, and the product is Windows-first.** `crates/engine-cli/src/launch.rs` and `crates/engine/src/observe/process.rs` hold `cfg(windows)` code. `crates/engine/Cargo.toml:21` adds `windows-sys` on Windows only. `.cargo/config.toml` applies `+crt-static` to the msvc target only. An Ubuntu-only check compiles none of it, so a Windows compile error surfaces during a release.

**F5 — the static C runtime promise has no gate.** Cargo ignores `rustflags` in `.cargo/config.toml` when `RUSTFLAGS` is set in the environment. `packaging/README.md:25` promises the game runs without the Visual C++ redistributable. `packaging/README.md:71` records the runtime presence as a fact, not as a pass or a failure. A dynamically linked setup file passes the clean-machine check.

**F6 — the content gate names a field that does not exist, and the fix breaks the build.** There is no `rules.pack_version`. The field is `schema_version` (`content/rules/default.json:2`), and nine packs each carry one. The engine refuses any other number: see `crates/engine/src/error.rs:41` and `crates/engine/tests/content.rs:102` ("schema_version 3; this build reads 4"). Bumping it on a tuning edit makes the shipped content unloadable until `RULES_VERSION` changes in code. A format version is not a content revision.

**F7 — the replay fixture has no policy and no home.** `web/replay-file.mjs:195` refuses any file whose protocol version differs from the page's version. A fixture from an older release fails by design at every protocol bump, and the plan does not say whether the test asserts a load or a clean refusal. `.gitignore:4` ignores `*.smfx`, with one exception at line 7 for `web/tests/data/`, so fixtures placed elsewhere stay untracked.

**F8 — the Linux glibc floor is unpinned and unmeasured.** `packaging/README.md:51` documents the floor as a property of the build machine. `packaging/unix/smoke.sh:59` records `ldd` and the glibc version as facts, never as checks. `ubuntu-22.04` is a deprecated hosted image; when the label goes, the floor rises silently and no check fails. The README's documented floor (glibc 2.39) also stops matching the shipped archive.

**F9 — `smoke.sh` is not an artifact-only check.** `packaging/unix/smoke.sh:130` runs `cargo test --release --locked -p engine-cli --test install_layout` from the repository folder. It needs the source tree, a toolchain, and a second release build. It works inside the release job. It cannot serve as a "tester smoke" for a person holding only the download.

**F10 — on the free plan the checks are advisory and the minutes are finite.** Branch protection returns 403, so no check blocks a merge; the gate is developer discipline. Actions minutes on a private free repository are metered, and Windows jobs bill at a higher rate, so an exhausted allowance stops releases. The Playwright suite appears in no stage, and `e2e/playwright.config.mjs:26` records the `scenario` project as more than eleven minutes of wall time with `workers: 1`. The shipped `web/` folder reaches players behind unit tests and one screenshot.

**F11 — the coverage floor has 0.3 points of headroom.** An 80% floor against a measured 80.30% baseline, on Linux only, with the Windows paths of F4 excluded, produces failures that carry no information.

**F12 — the heavy tests run once per cycle, outside the pipeline.** About 20 `#[ignore]` tests sit in `crates/engine/tests` and `crates/engine-cli/tests`. A realism regression can sit on `main` for a whole cycle.

**F13 — supporting files do not exist yet.** The tree holds no `.github/`, no `lefthook.yml`, and no `deny.toml`. `Cargo.toml:16` sets `repository = ""`, which `cargo-release` and the release notes both want. `committed` needs merge commits excluded, because the plan selects the merge-commit method.

**F14 — release workflow hygiene is absent.** The plan names no `workflow_dispatch`, no concurrency group, no least-privilege `permissions: contents: write`, no commit pinning for third-party actions, and no build provenance attestation. `packaging/README.md:57` states the setup file is unsigned, so provenance is the cheapest trust signal available.

**F15 — the installer has no upgrade path.** `packaging/windows/installer.nsi:63` copies the stage over an existing install with `File /r` and never removes the previous version. A content file deleted between two releases stays on the player's machine, and "fix forward" inherits that.

**F16 — two named checks carry little weight.** `npm audit` for `e2e/` guards one pinned development dependency, `@playwright/test 1.63.0`, which never ships; `web/` holds no `package.json`. Also, the workflow cannot name its four assets in advance, because each name embeds a version the workflow does not know, so it must glob `dist/`. `crates/engine-cli/tests/release_version.rs:87` guards only the two build scripts against a hardcoded version, so a workflow that hardcodes it escapes the guard.

## RECOMMENDATION

Do not ship this pipeline in this order. Fix F1 and F2, invert the publish sequence, then add the Windows PR job. Suggested order:

1. Make the NSIS version field accept a prerelease version, and prove it with a build.
2. Add a tag-to-version gate as the first job of the release workflow.
3. Build to a **draft** release; verify assets, hashes, version, and clean-machine evidence; publish last.
4. Add a Windows PR job that builds, tests, and asserts the static C runtime as a pass or a failure.
5. Replace the `rules.pack_version` gate with a content revision the engine does not refuse, or drop it.
6. Decide the replay compatibility policy before writing the fixture test, and track the fixtures.
7. Pin the Linux build environment, and gate the maximum required GLIBC symbol version.
8. Lower the coverage floor to a value with real headroom.
9. Put the ignored tests and the Playwright `viewer` project on a timer, inside the minutes budget.
10. Treat the PR checks as a pre-push hook first and as Actions second, because 403 means no Actions check blocks a merge.

The version scheme, the tag trigger, the asset set, the retain-everything rollback, and the remote realism gate all stand. The sequence and the two contract gates do not.
